output.brief: The rejects come from one combination: Arnholt resin run through dryer D5 on Press 5. D5's dew point has drifted to about −16 to −19 °C, and Arnholt arrives wetter (0.27–0.33% at the dryer inlet) than Quillan (0.11–0.14%). Through D5 it reaches the press at about 0.25–0.31%, above the 0.20% limit. That causes splay and latch cracks. Press 5 on Arnholt rejects about 9.9%. Press 5 on Quillan rejects 0.9%. Press 7 on Arnholt rejects 0.8%. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8%, against 10.4% through D5. The new operators are not the cause: they perform the same as experienced staff on each resin, and second shift looks worse only because all second-shift VX runs on Press 5. Don't discipline them, and don't drop Arnholt. One caveat: all Arnholt samples came from the north annex, so I can't say whether storage conditions explain the wetter inlet resin. Next steps: repair D5 (heater and desiccant) and verify −40 °C. Restore the alarm limit that was loosened in week 31. Keep Arnholt off D5 until then. Add a moisture check on every resin lot. Answer the 8D with this. Check annex storage separately and cheaply, with a conditioned-storage sample, before spending on renting space.
